request.spec:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each user can now pick which people-list columns their screen shows, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- A **Columns** box sits near the top of the sheet with one checkbox per column, `column-<name>`. Ticked means shown.
- Turning a column off removes its cell from every person row, and its table heading with it. The header, totals, summary and every other figure stay the same.
- The choice is saved per signed-in user, the same way the existing locale setting is. It stays in place when a sheet is loaded or re-loaded, and it applies whichever sheet is open. One user's choice doesn't affect anyone else's screen. Like the locale, it writes no audit line.
- A tick changes the screen straight away, and the saves go to the server one at a time, so quick clicks can't save out of order.

**One difference from the request:** the request lists 14 columns, but the test also switches off `excess` and expects its cell to disappear. So I made 15, with `excess` added.

**What changed**
- **Server:**
  - a new table, `V85__user_columns.sql`;
  - `GET` and `POST` endpoints at `/api/columns`;
  - their steps under `net.officefloor.hq.app.columns`. Column names it doesn't know are rejected.
- **Front end:** a new `features/columns/` holds the chooser, a hook that reads the user's choice, and a small `Col` wrapper. Each column's cell and heading in the existing row components are wrapped in `Col`.

**Not checked:** I couldn't type-check the front end on its own because TypeScript isn't installed in the project. The successful `bin/e2e` build is the only check on the new code.
